page: Amazon Web Services x1e.32xlarge is an x86_64 hypervisor-based instance belonging to the Memory Optimized family. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors operating at 2.3 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs via multithreading. A standout specification of the platform is its memory capacity, featuring 3904.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 30.5 GB per vCPU core. The server includes 3840 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. No graphical processing units (GPUs) are provisioned on this configuration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct performance trade-offs inherent to its legacy architecture. Single-core processing metrics, such as stress-ng single-core (727.39) and Geekbench single-core (862.0), place within the bottom 10 percent of recorded results. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression similarly register in the lower quartiles. However, high-concurrency and throughput benchmarks scale respectably: stress-ng multi-core (52044.34) and PassMark CPU (49221.05) maintain middle-tier averages. Cached small-block memory read bandwidth achieves a strong 3825.21 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads attain 201.38 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the x1e.32xlarge prioritizes extreme RAM footprint over modern per-core compute efficiency. While the older Xeon v3 architecture results in reduced instruction throughput per core relative to newer processor generations, the massive memory density avoids the need to distribute oversized memory models across multiple cluster nodes. This profile makes the instance viable specifically for memory-bound workloads, large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or massive Redis deployments, real-time analytics, and substantial database operations requiring massive memory residency.
description: Amazon Web Services x1e.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores, powered by 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors on an x86_64 architecture. Designed around extensive memory allocations, it delivers 3904.0 GB of RAM alongside 3840 GB of bundled local SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated accelerators or GPUs are included. Performance profiles show constrained single-core compute speeds, evidenced by low single-thread Geekbench and compression figures, balanced by strong uncached memory bandwidth of 201.38 GB/sec and respectable multi-core metric outputs. The dense memory-to-core ratio of 30.5 GB per core favors monolithic, RAM-heavy environments over instruction-heavy computational jobs. It is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching instances, and memory-intensive data processing workloads.
